svg.text: Servo on a knob, then a pan-tilt
LP-MSPM0G3507, seen from above, USB unplugged. Add the wires in the numbered order; each number sits at both ends of its wire and in the list below. The schematic shows the same circuit in symbols.
J1 and J2 are the outer columns, J3 and J4 the inner ones; pin 1, 21, 40 and 20 are at the USB end.
Wire colours: red 3.3 V, orange 5 V, black ground; every other colour is one signal.

g.text: Breadboard: holes a to e, and f to j, in one column are joined; each long rail is joined end to end.
Column 1 is at this end; rails and holes count up toward the top.
3 to left ground rail, hole 3 (LaunchPad ground)
3 from right ground rail, hole 3 (power module ground)
Wires, in the order you add them
Ground rail (blue, hole 2) to J2 pin 20 (GND)
Bottom ground rail, hole 3 (power module ground) to Top ground rail, hole 3 (LaunchPad ground)
Part 1: one servo on a knob
Knob 1 outer pin, breadboard j6 to 3V3 rail
Knob 1 outer pin, breadboard j10 to Ground rail
Knob 1 middle pin, breadboard j8 to J1 pin 2 (PA25)
Knob 2 outer pin, breadboard j16 to 3V3 rail
Knob 2 outer pin, breadboard j20 to Ground rail
Knob 2 middle pin, breadboard j18 to J1 pin 6 (PB24)
Part 1: one servo on a knob
Servo 1 brown (ground) to Bottom ground rail
Servo 1 red (5 V) to Bottom 5 V rail
Servo 2 brown (ground) to Bottom ground rail
Servo 2 red (5 V) to Bottom 5 V rail
Knob 1 (pan): one outer pin in g6, middle pin (wiper) in g8, other outer pin in g10
Knob 2 (tilt): one outer pin in g16, middle pin (wiper) in g18, other outer pin in g20
Breadboard power module: + pin in bp1, − pin in bm1
Servo 1: beside the breadboard, pins toward the wires
Servo 2: beside the breadboard, pins toward the wires
The breadboard power module takes 6.5 to 12 V on its barrel jack or 5 V on its USB; set both jumpers to 5 V; its ground must join the LaunchPad ground.
A hobby servo can draw over 500 mA when it stalls: power it from the breadboard power module, never from the LaunchPad kit's 5 V pin.
Then plug in USB, run the build, and expect
Pan follows knob 1; tilt follows knob 2. Neither servo makes the LaunchPad reset.
The same circuit as a schematic

svg.text: Fox Red Labs. Pins from the build's pin table, the one the program is built from; the 3D build on the page shows the same wiring step by step. Board picture: TI SLAU873E, figure 1-1.
